mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in household demand, which reduces economic activity and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above 63% for six months signals a tighter labor market, which boosts wage pressures and inflation, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth outpaces inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive trend in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) quarter-over-quarter for four consecutive quarters signals robust demand growth, which supports corporate earnings and justifies positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of quarters with sustained GDPC1 growth.
